newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht under pressure, seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht under pressure, seen volatile.

text.p: Thailand's baht came under renewed pressure on Monday amid continued turmoil in regional currencies and analysts expect further falls on concern over domestic political problems.
The baht fell sharply against the dollar in early Monday trade on a spillover of the rupiah's losses after Indonesia's move to float the rupiah.
By midday the baht had retreated to 31.90/32.00 per dollar from 31.75/31.95 near the close of trade on Friday.

"The passing of the mid-August deadline put some pressure on the baht by reducing demand to sell dollar for baht (to cover their forward positions)," Ali Seng, regional economist at MMS International, told Reuters.
Analysts said most three-month forward positions had been taken out during speculative attacks on the baht in mid-May which prompted the Bank of Thailand to impose capital controls.
The central bank imposed a two-tier foreign exchange market -- one onshore and one offshore - which choked baht supplies to offshore speculators and led to a scramble to cover forward contracts.
Seng said politics also affected market sentiment with Friday's cabinet reshuffle giving rise to some jitters.
Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh brought a respected conservative economist and a business tycoon into his cabinet in a bid to bolster his government's sagging image.
Chavalit also appointed former finance minister Virabongsa Ramangkura as deputy prime minister in charge of finance and fiscal affairs.
Some analysts expressed disappointment at the reshuffle, saying it fell short of expectations, while some members of the press and academics have called for Chavalit's resignation.
They say his coalition government has failed to deal with the country's economic woes.
Analysts said sluggish inflows of foreign funds and weak exports have reduced dollar supplies and compounded the baht's weakness.
"As long as no fresh funds flow in and the export sector remains sluggish, the baht can fall further," said one senior dealer at a European bank.
In the long term, the baht will be boosted by the International Monetary Fund-brokered $16.7 billion support package, analysts said.
The IMF board is expected to give final approval of the package this week.
